hero.headline: US Stocks Tumble as Tech Selloff and Rate Hike Fears Hit Markets
hero.body:
US stock markets suffered their worst decline of the year on Friday as investors fled technology stocks and reassessed interest rate expectations following stronger-than-expected jobs data. The Nasdaq fell 4.2 percent, marking its steepest single-day drop since April 2025, while the S&P 500 declined more than 2.6 percent, ending nine consecutive weeks of gains.

The selloff centered on chip and technology companies, with semiconductor stocks experiencing sharp declines. Broadcom and Intel shares dropped along with other major chip manufacturers including AMD, Micron, Qualcomm, and Super Micro. The technology-heavy Nasdaq bore the brunt of selling pressure as investors rotated away from artificial intelligence and megacap technology stocks that had driven much of the market's recent gains.

The market decline came after the Labor Department reported that US employers added 172,000 jobs in May, substantially exceeding economist forecasts. The robust hiring data prompted traders to increase their expectations that the Federal Reserve may resume raising interest rates to combat persistent inflation. Higher interest rates typically reduce the appeal of growth-oriented technology stocks, whose valuations depend heavily on future earnings.

Bitcoin also fell below $60,000 for the first time since the November 2024 election, reflecting a broader shift in investor sentiment away from digital assets and toward other investment opportunities.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which includes fewer technology companies, posted modest gains and reached a record level, suggesting investors sought refuge in more traditional industrial and financial stocks. Market analysts said the divergence demonstrated that some sectors could continue performing well even as the technology trade cooled. The sharp contrast between the Dow's performance and the Nasdaq's decline highlighted the concentrated nature of recent market weakness in the technology sector.

The selloff underscores ongoing tensions for investors balancing inflation concerns against growth prospects. While strong employment data signals economic resilience, it also raises the likelihood of additional Fed rate increases that could slow business expansion. This dynamic has created uncertainty about whether technology stocks, which soared on optimism about artificial intelligence applications, can sustain their momentum.

Analysts noted that the market rotation suggests investors are reassessing their strategy after months of technology dominance. Some are moving capital into defensive sectors and traditional value stocks that typically perform better in higher interest rate environments. The employment report effectively reset market expectations about the Fed's path forward, with traders now pricing in a greater probability of rate increases rather than the cuts that had been anticipated earlier in the year.

The day's trading illustrated how sensitive markets remain to economic data and Federal Reserve policy signals. As investors digest the implications of stronger hiring for inflation and interest rates, the question remains whether the technology sector's recent strength has run its course or if this represents merely a temporary pullback before renewed gains.

cards.headline: CDC warns Ebola outbreak could sicken over 20,000 without immediate action
cards.body:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention released new modeling showing that the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could sicken more than 20,000 people in the next three months without prompt intervention. The projection places the outbreak among the most severe Ebola crises on record if the situation continues unchecked.

Since the outbreak was identified in mid-May, the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola has caused 344 confirmed cases and 60 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, along with 15 confirmed cases and one death in neighboring Uganda. The virus may have begun spreading much earlier than initially recognized. World Health Organization director Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the outbreak could have started as early as January, giving the virus a significant head start before detection and response efforts began.

The CDC's warning emphasizes that this projection is not inevitable. Health officials stress that rapid implementation of containment measures can prevent the outbreak from reaching such catastrophic levels. Standard response strategies include contact tracing, isolating infected patients, ensuring safe burial practices, and strengthening healthcare infrastructure in affected areas.

Contact tracing represents a critical challenge to containing the spread. Currently, only about 45 percent of contacts are being followed up in affected regions. Tedros stated that reaching above 90 percent contact tracing would be essential to getting ahead of the outbreak. The low contact tracing rates stem from multiple obstacles, including insecurity and displacement in Ituri province, the most heavily impacted area.

Community mistrust poses another significant barrier to response efforts. Tedros reported that some community leaders expressed skepticism about whether Ebola is real, while others worried that outbreak response activities would divert resources from other critical health services. Additionally, blanket travel restrictions imposed by some countries, including the United States, are disrupting supply chains and hindering the international response.

Laboratory and diagnostic capacity remains limited in the most affected areas and neighboring regions. This capacity gap contributed to a testing backlog that caused a sudden drop in reported suspected cases from over 1,000 to 116 as officials worked through pending test results to confirm or rule out infections.

Despite the absence of a vaccine or treatment specifically for the Bundibugyo strain, health officials note a reason for cautious hope. Six people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and two in Uganda have recovered from Ebola, demonstrating that survival is possible with access to proper care and early treatment. The key to recovery is ensuring that infected individuals reach health facilities promptly after symptoms appear.

Public health experts view the CDC's modeling as an urgent call to action for the international community. The three-month timeline underscores how quickly the situation could deteriorate without coordinated global response efforts focused on containment and community engagement.

cards.headline: Iran Launches Drone Strike on Kuwait Airport, Hits US Military Positions
cards.body:
Iran carried out a drone attack on Kuwait International Airport that resulted in casualties, according to multiple reports from local media and international sources. The strike targeted US Fifth Fleet headquarters and an airbase at the airport, Reuters reported. Kuwait released surveillance footage of the attack.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched the operation against US military positions in Kuwait, local media reported. The Wall Street Journal described the incident as part of a skirmish between the United States and Iran that resulted in the deadly drone attack. The airport serves as a dual civilian and military facility.

The attack comes amid renewed ceasefire negotiations between Israel and Lebanon, CBS News reported. The timing suggests heightened regional tensions involving multiple parties in the Middle East. Kuwait, a US ally that hosts American military personnel and facilities, has historically maintained a careful balancing act in the region.

The surveillance video released by Kuwaiti authorities shows the moment of the drone strike at the international airport. AP News confirmed that Kuwait made the footage public, though the reports did not specify the extent of damage or provide detailed casualty figures from the attack.

The strike on US military positions marks a significant escalation in tensions between Washington and Tehran. The US Fifth Fleet, headquartered in Bahrain, maintains operations throughout the Persian Gulf region, including facilities in Kuwait. Iran has previously threatened American military installations in the Gulf in response to various geopolitical disputes, but direct attacks on US positions represent a notable increase in hostilities.

cards.headline: US Employers Added 172,000 Jobs in May, Exceeding Forecasts
cards.teaser: The US economy added 172,000 jobs last month, beating expectations and extending a vigorous hiring pace.
cards.body:
US employers added 172,000 jobs in May, marking the third consecutive month of job growth. The unemployment rate remained stable at 4.3%, demonstrating underlying strength in the labor market despite rising inflation and geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East.

Much of the job growth came from restaurants, bars, and hotels. However, wage gains have softened and likely failed to keep pace with inflation, presenting a mixed picture for workers despite the robust headline employment numbers.

cards.headline: Senate completes 18-hour voting session on immigration enforcement package
cards.teaser: The Senate concluded a marathon vote-a-rama on immigration enforcement legislation after nearly a full day of continuous voting.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a $70 billion immigration enforcement funding bill following an 18-hour overnight voting session. The Republican-backed legislation provides funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Border Patrol over the next three years.

The extended vote-a-rama session is a procedural feature of budget reconciliation bills that allows senators to propose unlimited amendments. Lawmakers worked through the night to complete votes on the enforcement package, with each individual vote taking only minutes.

cards.headline: States Prepare Antitrust Lawsuit Against Paramount-Warner Bros Merger
cards.teaser: Multiple US states are preparing legal action to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros.
cards.body:
Several US states are preparing to file a lawsuit challenging Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. on antitrust grounds, according to sources familiar with the matter. The legal challenge comes amid ongoing debate about media consolidation and market concentration in the entertainment industry.

A Paramount lawyer defended the deal, claiming that some opponents hold antisemitic views, while the company's antitrust chief criticized what he called fear-mongering and partisan politics surrounding the transaction. Paramount has requested that an existing lawsuit seeking to block the merger be dismissed, calling it an attempt to politicize antitrust litigation.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutor opens election fraud investigations in California after Trump allegations
cards.body:
A federal prosecutor in California announced multiple investigations into alleged voter fraud following accusations by President Trump that Democrats engaged in misconduct during this week's primary elections. Bill Essayli, the first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, revealed the probes on Friday without disclosing specifics about what allegations are being examined.

The announcement came as California completed its gubernatorial primary election, where Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton competed for their party nominations to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Trump made public accusations of election fraud against Democrats in the state after primary voting concluded.

The Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles on Friday as Trump continued to claim that California Democrats were "rigging" the results. State officials have rejected the allegations, though the delay in election results has prompted concerns about misinformation regarding California's election integrity.

Election officials have explained that counting votes in California is taking longer than in other states due to the volume of ballots and processing procedures. Experts have warned that ballot counting could extend for weeks or even a month before final results are determined in the governor's race, the Los Angeles mayoral election, and congressional contests.

Essayli's announcement represents a notable development in the ongoing tensions between the Trump administration and California's Democratic leadership. The Central District of California, one of four federal judicial districts in the state, covers a significant portion of Southern California including Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, and Ventura counties.

Federal election fraud investigations are relatively uncommon and typically require substantial evidence of organized attempts to interfere with voting processes or ballot counting. The Justice Department has not disclosed information about the specific nature of the fraud allegations or which aspects of the primary election are under investigation.

The timing of the investigations, announced immediately after the primary and following presidential accusations, represents an unusual convergence of federal law enforcement activity and electoral politics. California has traditionally been a Democratic stronghold, and disputes between state officials and the Trump administration have become a consistent element of recent political dynamics. Trump has long promoted election conspiracy theories and made similar claims of fraud in previous elections without providing evidence.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Drone Explodes in Romanian Port After Russian Jamming
cards.teaser: A Ukrainian naval drone detonated in a Romanian Black Sea port after Russian electronic warfare systems pushed it off course.
cards.body:
A Ukrainian maritime drone detonated at a Romanian port on the Black Sea. Ukraine attributed the incident to Russian electronic warfare jamming that diverted the drone from its intended target.

The explosion occurred in NATO territory, as Romania is a member of the alliance. The incident highlights how the conflict's effects are extending beyond Ukraine's borders, with Russian electronic warfare capabilities disrupting Ukrainian military operations throughout the war.

cards.headline: Putin Rejects Zelensky's Call for Direct Peace Talks
cards.teaser: Russian President Vladimir Putin said there is no point in meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to discuss ending the war.
cards.body:
Putin has rejected Volodymyr Zelensky's offer to meet for face-to-face negotiations on ending the Ukraine war. Speaking at the St. Petersburg economic forum, Putin described Zelensky's open letter as rude and said he saw "no point" in such a meeting. He refused to use Zelensky's name when discussing the proposal.

Putin reaffirmed Russia's commitment to achieving its war objectives in Ukraine, including seizing all of the eastern Donbas region. His rejection signals that Russia intends to continue pursuing its military goals rather than pursue peace negotiations.

cards.headline: Astronauts Return to ISS After Sheltering During Russian Repair Attempt
cards.teaser: Five astronauts returned to their regular quarters on the International Space Station after taking shelter during a Russian effort to fix an air leak.
cards.body:
Two air leaks were discovered in the Zveda module's transfer chamber during a pressurization procedure. Russian specialists detected the leaks while pressurizing the transfer chamber to the ISS, prompting NASA to order five astronauts to prepare for possible evacuation as a precaution.

The repair work has since paused, and the astronauts have returned to the station. The incident highlights ongoing air leak concerns on the aging International Space Station, particularly in its Russian segments.

cards.headline: France Opens Investigation Into Israeli Treatment of Gaza Flotilla Activists
cards.teaser: French authorities launched an inquiry after activists detained by Israel while trying to reach Gaza reported abuse in custody.
cards.body:
France has initiated an investigation into allegations of abuse against activists detained while attempting to reach Gaza by sea. The flotilla participants reported mistreatment during their time in Israeli custody.

Israeli authorities have rejected the abuse claims. The investigation reflects ongoing tensions between France and Israel regarding the treatment of individuals involved in the pro-Palestinian mission.

cards.headline: EU Leaders Signal Montenegro Could Join by 2028
cards.teaser: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Montenegro is within reach of EU membership by 2028 following a summit on Balkan expansion.
cards.body:
EU leaders gathered at a summit in Montenegro's coastal town of Tivat to discuss accelerating the bloc's enlargement process. Commission President von der Leyen stated that Montenegro is "within reach" of joining by 2028, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz emphasized that the EU must demonstrate both its capability and willingness to accept new members.

The push to speed up expansion reflects a broader strategic shift. EU officials aim to make the enlargement process "faster and more credible" while addressing geopolitical concerns about Russian and Chinese influence in the Western Balkans region. Montenegro has been a candidate for membership for years, and this accelerated timeline would represent a significant change in the bloc's approach.

cards.headline: Iran's National Soccer Team Receives US Visas Days Before World Cup
cards.teaser: Iranian players were granted entry to the United States just days before the World Cup begins, ending months of uncertainty about their participation.
cards.body:
The Iranian national team received visas after prolonged doubts over whether they would be allowed to compete in the tournament hosted by the United States. Many staff members were denied entry, according to reports. The visa approvals came with little time before the competition starts.

The situation highlights ongoing diplomatic tensions between Washington and Tehran. The World Cup, scheduled to begin in days, will now include the Iranian squad despite the visa complications. The denial of visas to support staff may affect the team's preparations and operations during the tournament.

cards.headline: National Park Service ranger dies after falling into crevasse on Denali
cards.teaser: A climbing ranger from Washington state died during a patrol on Alaska's Mount McKinley, marking the fourth death on the peak this season.
cards.body:
A National Park Service ranger from Washington state died after falling into a crevasse on Denali, also known as Mount McKinley, North America's tallest peak. The ranger was conducting a patrol on the mountain when the accident occurred.

The death marks the fourth fatality on the mountain this season, according to reports. Park service officials confirmed the ranger's death but additional details about the circumstances of the fall were not immediately provided.

cards.headline: Murder trial continues in fatal stabbing at Texas high school track meet
cards.teaser: Teenage witnesses testified in the trial of Karmelo Anthony, a 19-year-old accused of stabbing a fellow high school student at a Frisco ISD track meet.
cards.body:
The murder trial of 19-year-old Karmelo Anthony continued into its fourth day with testimony from teenage witnesses who were present at the Frisco ISD track meet. Jurors were shown arrest and bodycam footage as evidence. Anthony is accused of fatally stabbing 17-year-old Austin Metcalf during the track meet on April 2, 2025, at Kuykendall Stadium.

The case has drawn national attention amid broader discussions about racial tensions, with Anthony being Black and Metcalf being white. Prosecutors are presenting evidence about the confrontation that led to Metcalf's death, with witnesses describing the events surrounding the stabbing.

cards.headline: British actor Anthony Head dies at 72
cards.teaser: Anthony Head, known for roles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso, died from complications of pneumonia.
cards.body:
British actor Anthony Head has died at age 72 from pneumonia complications. Head rose to prominence in the 1980s through Nescafe advertisements before building a successful television career spanning multiple decades.

Head was best known for his roles in popular series including Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso. He also appeared in Merlin and Little Britain, showcasing his versatility across dramatic and comedic productions in both British and American television.

cards.headline: FBI fires analysts who wrote memo on radical Catholic ideology
cards.teaser: The FBI terminated analysts responsible for a memo that addressed radical Catholic ideology, which had drawn criticism.
cards.body:
The FBI dismissed analysts who authored an internal memo addressing radical Catholic ideology. The memo had generated controversy after its contents became public.

The firings follow scrutiny of the document and its characterization of certain Catholic groups. The memo had raised concerns about the bureau's approach to monitoring religious communities.

cards.headline: Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool refilled after repainting project
cards.teaser: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is being refilled after President Trump ordered it painted in what he called American flag blue.
cards.body:
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C., is refilling following a repainting project ordered by President Trump. The pool was coated with a color called "American flag blue," and the renovation work reportedly cost millions of dollars.

Since the project's completion, visitors have questioned the visible impact of the work. Many observers note that the changes to the pool's appearance are subtle compared to its previous look.

cards.headline: Astronauts return to main ISS areas after air leak repair attempt
cards.teaser: Five astronauts sheltered in safe areas of the International Space Station during a Russian attempt to repair an air leak in a tunnel section.
cards.body:
Two air leaks were discovered in the Zveza module's transfer chamber during a pressurization procedure. Russian specialists with the station's main operations team detected the leaks while pressurizing the chamber to connect with ISS systems.

NASA ordered five astronauts to prepare for possible evacuation as a precautionary measure. The astronauts have now returned to normal operations aboard the station as the repair attempt was paused.

cards.headline: Google Strikes $920 Million Monthly Cloud Deal with SpaceX
cards.teaser: Google agreed to pay SpaceX nearly $1 billion per month for cloud computing capacity.
cards.body:
Google will pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing capacity at xAI data centers. A Google representative attributed the deal to unexpected demand for the company's recently launched AI products.

The agreement represents a major computing contract for the cloud infrastructure sector and provides SpaceX with a significant new revenue stream beyond its space launch and satellite internet operations.

cards.headline: S&P 500 Denies SpaceX Early Entry to Index
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 will not change its rules to allow SpaceX into the benchmark index ahead of standard eligibility requirements.
cards.body:
S&P rejected a request to modify its index inclusion rules that would have allowed SpaceX to join the S&P 500 earlier than normal procedures permit. The decision also affects other major companies preparing for initial public offerings, including OpenAI and Anthropic, which had sought similar treatment.

The ruling means SpaceX and other mega IPOs will face the standard waiting period before becoming eligible for inclusion in the benchmark index. Elon Musk has described SpaceX as entering a massive growth phase, but the company will need to meet conventional eligibility criteria before index funds tracking the S&P 500 can invest.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Drops Below $60,000 for First Time Since 2024 Election
cards.teaser: Bitcoin fell below $60,000, reaching its lowest level since November 2024.
cards.body:
Bitcoin has fallen below $60,000, reaching its lowest level since October 2024. The decline marks a significant shift in the cryptocurrency market as investors redirect their focus elsewhere.

The drop reflects broader capital movements in the investment landscape, with traders moving funds toward alternative opportunities including artificial intelligence stocks and other emerging sectors. This reallocation has reduced demand for Bitcoin amid increased competition for investor attention.

cards.headline: Chip Stocks Lead Semiconductor Sector Decline
cards.teaser: Broadcom and Intel shares fell sharply as the chip sector selloff continued.
cards.body:
Broadcom and Intel stocks dropped as part of a broader semiconductor sector selloff that traders said has not yet run its course. The decline spread across major chip manufacturers, with AMD, Micron, Qualcomm, and Super Micro among the companies seeing significant losses.

Broadcom's quarterly results sparked the initial wave of selling across the semiconductor industry. Intel, AMD, and Micron shares later trimmed some losses but remained substantially down for the session. The selloff reflected investor concerns about valuations in the chip sector following a prolonged rally driven by artificial intelligence demand.

hero.headline: Creative speaker vulnerability allows PC infection over Bluetooth without user interaction
hero.body:
Security researchers have discovered a vulnerability in Creative's Sound Blaster Katana V2X speaker that allows attackers to infect computers through Bluetooth without any user action. The exploit, called Pwnd Blaster, targets the speaker's firmware and can compromise connected PCs remotely.

The vulnerability works through the speaker's Bluetooth connection to a computer. Once a speaker is within range, an attacker can exploit weaknesses in how the device communicates with the host system. The attack does not require the user to click anything, open files, or interact with the speaker in any way. The speaker simply needs to be connected to the computer via USB and have Bluetooth enabled.

Creative, the manufacturer of the Sound Blaster Katana V2X, does not consider the behavior a security vulnerability. The company has not indicated whether it plans to issue a firmware update or take other remedial action. The speaker retails for approximately $300 and is marketed as a premium PC audio solution.

Security professionals have expressed concern about the discovery. The ability to compromise a system through a trusted peripheral device represents a significant attack vector that many users would not anticipate. Unlike traditional malware that requires downloading suspicious files or visiting compromised websites, this exploit leverages hardware that users intentionally connect to their systems.

The revelation has prompted some computer users to reconsider their connected devices. Experts recommend that users disconnect Bluetooth speakers when not in use and maintain updated firmware for all peripheral devices. The incident highlights the expanding attack surface created by the growing number of connected devices in typical computing environments. As more hardware incorporates wireless connectivity, the potential for similar exploits in other devices remains a concern for cybersecurity professionals.

cards.headline: IBM accused of covering up multiple data breaches from mid-2010s
cards.teaser: A former cybersecurity executive filed a lawsuit alleging IBM and two subsidiaries suffered breaches that were never disclosed.
cards.body:
IBM and two subsidiary companies experienced data breaches in the mid-2010s, according to a lawsuit filed by a former cybersecurity executive. The whistleblower alleges that IBM was aware of the security incidents but failed to disclose them and actively concealed them.

The former cyber executive brought the complaint against IBM regarding the company's handling of these breaches and its decision not to inform affected parties or regulators about the incidents.

cards.headline: ISS crew returns after air leak repair attempt triggers shelter procedure
cards.teaser: Five astronauts sheltered in place while Russian crew attempted to repair a tunnel leak on the International Space Station.
cards.body:
Two air leaks were discovered in the Zvezda module's transfer chamber during pressurization work on the International Space Station. Russian specialists detected the leaks while preparing to pressurize the transfer chamber connecting to the ISS.

NASA ordered five astronauts to prepare for a possible evacuation as a safety precaution while repairs were underway. The crew has since returned to normal operations aboard the station.

cards.headline: Small modular nuclear reactor reaches criticality in first test
cards.teaser: Antares, a nuclear startup, achieved criticality with its small modular reactor design, though it is not yet ready to generate power.
cards.body:
A small modular nuclear reactor from startup Antares reached criticality during its first test. The milestone represents a key step in developing smaller, more flexible nuclear power systems.

Criticality occurs when a nuclear reactor sustains a chain reaction. The Antares reactor is not yet ready to generate electricity for commercial use. Small modular reactors are designed to be built in factories and transported to sites, potentially reducing construction costs and deployment time compared to traditional large-scale nuclear plants.

cards.headline: FDA unable to identify cause of baby botulism outbreak
cards.teaser: Federal regulators still do not know what caused a botulism outbreak affecting infants or how to prevent future cases.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has not determined the source of a baby botulism outbreak. The agency also lacks guidance on preventing similar incidents in the future.

Three companies involved in the investigation have blamed each other for the contamination. Botulism is a rare but serious illness caused by toxins that attack the nervous system. Infant botulism occurs when babies ingest spores that produce toxins in the intestines.

cards.headline: Capcom announces remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica for 2027
cards.teaser: The survival horror game will be released as Resident Evil Veronica for Nintendo Switch 2 and other platforms next year.
cards.body:
Capcom revealed a remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica, retitled simply as Resident Evil Veronica. The game is scheduled to launch in 2027 for Nintendo Switch 2 and other platforms.

Code Veronica originally released in 2000 and continued the story of Claire Redfield. The remake follows Capcom's recent pattern of updating classic Resident Evil titles with modern graphics and gameplay systems. The company has successfully remade Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 in recent years.

cards.headline: Guild Wars 3 revealed with beta planned for fall 2027
cards.teaser: ArenaNet announced the next installment in its MMORPG franchise for PC and PlayStation 5.
cards.body:
Guild Wars 3 was officially announced at Summer Game Fest. The massively multiplayer online game will launch on PC and PlayStation 5, with a beta test starting in fall 2027.

ArenaNet is developing the game as what it calls a modern evolution of the MMORPG genre. Guild Wars 2 continues to operate and will receive ongoing support alongside the development of the new title. The original Guild Wars launched in 2005, with Guild Wars 2 following in 2012.

hero.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams for Jared Verse and three draft picks
hero.body:
The Cleveland Browns have traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft selections. The deal reshapes both franchises as the Browns continue their roster rebuild and the Rams pursue another championship run.

Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since Cleveland selected him first overall in 2017, he has established himself as one of the league's elite defensive players. He leads all players drafted since 2017 with 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures, and 149 tackles for loss. In 2025, Garrett set the single-season sack record with 23, earning All-Pro recognition even as the Browns finished 5-12 and missed the playoffs for the second consecutive year.

Garrett had requested a trade in 2024 after the Browns struggled to a 3-14 record, expressing his desire to play for a championship contender. Despite this request, he signed a four-year, $160 million extension one month later, making him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time. The deal includes $122.8 million guaranteed and an average annual salary of $40 million.

The trade became possible after the Browns and Garrett agreed to modify his contract in March, deferring option payments to the 2026-28 seasons. A payment originally due March 28 was moved to near the start of the regular season, providing the financial flexibility necessary for the move.

Browns general manager Andrew Berry acknowledged the difficult decision in a statement. "As discussions intensified we were stuck at a legitimate crossroads: do we hold on to a truly generational player who has become the identity of our team, or do we make the difficult decision that we think is best for the organization over the long run?" Berry said.

The Browns received a 2027 first-round selection, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round selection along with Verse. The 25-year-old linebacker was a first-round draft pick by the Rams in 2024 and earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. He has recorded 12 career sacks and 22 tackles for loss while also earning Pro Bowl selection this past season.

For the Rams, acquiring Garrett adds elite pass rush talent to a defense that lost to the eventual champion Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC championship game. The franchise has a history of making significant trades to improve its roster, including the 2021 blockbuster quarterback trade with Detroit that brought Matthew Stafford to Los Angeles. Stafford led the Rams to a Super Bowl victory in his first season and won the Associated Press NFL MVP award last season. Garrett's arrival marks the first time the reigning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year will be teammates.

cards.headline: Yankees place Aaron Judge on injured list
cards.teaser: The Yankees have placed outfielder Aaron Judge on the injured list, forcing the team to address how it will replace his production.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge has been placed on the injured list by the New York Yankees, removing the team's top offensive threat from the lineup. Judge had been attempting to play through pain before the injury forced him to the sidelines. The slugger expressed disappointment after his worst fear was realized.

The Yankees now face questions about how to compensate for Judge's absence and whether their remaining offense can sustain them through the period he is unavailable. The injury also carries implications for the American League East race and could influence the team's approach to the MLB trade deadline.

cards.headline: Dana White declares Alex Pereira greatest fighter ever with win over Ciryl Gane
cards.teaser: UFC president Dana White said Alex Pereira would surpass Jon Jones as the greatest fighter of all time if he defeats Ciryl Gane.
cards.body:
UFC president Dana White stated that Alex Pereira will eclipse Jon Jones as the greatest fighter in mixed martial arts history if he defeats heavyweight Ciryl Gane. The bout is scheduled to take place at UFC Freedom 250 at the White House. Pereira is making his heavyweight debut and has revealed his expected weight for the fight.

Gane has enlisted multiple fighters from the GLORY kickboxing organization to help prepare for Pereira's striking style. The French fighter is competing despite the political backdrop of the event. White's declaration counters commentator Joe Rogan's characterization of the White House event as a gimmick.

cards.headline: Bears board votes to pursue new stadium in Hammond, Indiana
cards.teaser: The Chicago Bears board of directors voted to advance plans for a new NFL stadium in Hammond, Indiana, moving the franchise across state lines.
cards.body:
The Chicago Bears board of directors has voted to push forward with development of a new stadium in Hammond, Indiana. The decision moves the franchise closer to leaving Illinois and relocating to northwest Indiana. The Bears released a statement confirming the board's vote to advance the stadium project.

Chicago businesses have expressed concern over the plan, with some saying they are hurt by the prospect of the team departing the city. The move would mark a historic shift for the franchise, which has played in Chicago since its founding. Hammond officials are working with the team on the development.

cards.headline: Scotland maintain World Cup qualifying lead amid Erin Cuthbert injury concern
cards.teaser: Scotland stayed atop their Women's World Cup qualifying group on goal difference from Belgium but face uncertainty over midfielder Erin Cuthbert's fitness.
cards.body:
Scotland remains top of their Women's World Cup qualifying group on goal difference ahead of Belgium. However, the team faces uncertainty surrounding midfielder Erin Cuthbert, who has suffered an injury that could prove serious.

Cuthbert has been instrumental for Scotland throughout their qualifying campaign. Her potential absence would be a significant blow to their hopes of securing automatic qualification for the World Cup.

cards.headline: Iran players receive US visas for World Cup matches
cards.teaser: Iranian national team players have been granted US visas to participate in the 2026 World Cup despite ongoing diplomatic tensions.
cards.body:
The Iranian national soccer team has secured US visas to compete in the 2026 World Cup, a significant development given the strained diplomatic relations between the two countries. The approval allows the team to participate in the tournament despite ongoing tensions.

The visa approvals come as many Iranian fans face barriers to attending matches in person due to visa rejections and the broader conflict between the nations. Los Angeles' Iranian community, known as Tehrangeles, now has a team to follow in the tournament.

cards.headline: Real Madrid prepare bid for Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise
cards.teaser: Real Madrid are lining up a 130 million euro move for Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise as the summer transfer window heats up.
cards.body:
Real Madrid will launch a €150m bid for Bayern Munich's Michael Olise if president Florentino Pérez wins re-election this weekend. Olise is set to be the club's top target in the summer transfer window, and has been watched by potential new manager José Mourinho.

In other transfer news, Arne Slot has turned down an offer from Fulham following his dismissal by Liverpool. Newcastle United are close to completing their first signing of the summer window.

hero.headline: British Actor Anthony Head Dies at 72
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72 from complications due to pneumonia. His daughters Emily and Daisy Head confirmed his passing in a statement, saying he "passed away peacefully, surrounded by his family."

Head's most iconic role was as the school librarian and mentor to Sarah Michelle Gellar's character throughout Buffy the Vampire Slayer's seven-season run from 1997 to 2003. The character of Giles, known as a "Watcher," became a beloved figure among fans of the supernatural series. Creator Joss Whedon had long planned a spinoff called Ripper that would have explored Giles' younger years, though the project never came to fruition.

Beyond his work on Buffy, Head had a remarkably diverse career spanning decades across theatre, film, and television. He appeared in the BBC sketch comedy show Little Britain, where he played a British prime minister constantly fawned over by a flirtatious assistant. He also featured in the BBC's Merlin series and took film roles in The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie.

More recently, Head played Rupert Mannion, a former football club owner, in the Apple TV+ series Ted Lasso, where he worked alongside co-creator Jason Sudeikis and was praised for their on-screen chemistry.

Head was born in Camden, London, to artistic parents. His father founded the documentary production company Verity Films, while his mother was an actor who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother was also an actor known for his lead role in the 1971 film Sunday Bloody Sunday. This creative environment shaped Head's early life, with his mother making elaborate dressing-up costumes that completely immersed the young actor in character play.

He began his professional career on stage, starring in a 1978 West End revival of Godspell. His theatre work became a cornerstone of his career, including roles in productions of Chess, where he played Freddie Trumper, and The Rocky Horror Show, where he starred as Dr. Frank-N-Furter in 1990. In the 1980s, he also sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box, appearing on their 1986 debut album.

Head gained significant recognition in Britain and America through Nescafé Gold Blend television advertisements that featured a slow-burn romance between two neighbours. When he took the Buffy role, he relocated to Los Angeles while his partner Sarah and two young daughters remained in England. He made frequent trips home, arranging his filming schedule to allow visits every three to four weeks.

His daughters remembered him as someone who loved his work and felt fortunate to work with talented colleagues across productions spanning several decades. They noted that his legacy would continue through the shows he appeared in and the audiences who cherish them.

cards.headline: Actor James Handy Fatally Stabbed in Los Angeles
cards.teaser: Character actor James Handy was killed in a stabbing at his Tarzana home, with his girlfriend's son charged with murder.
cards.body:
Veteran actor James Handy died following a stabbing at his home in Tarzana, Los Angeles. The 81-year-old was found unconscious in his front yard on Wednesday morning with multiple stab wounds to the chest.

The son of Handy's girlfriend has been arrested and charged with murder in connection with the attack. Handy had a long career in Hollywood, appearing in films including Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, along with numerous television shows.

cards.headline: Reed Hastings Departs Netflix Board After 25 Years
cards.teaser: Netflix co-founder and former CEO Reed Hastings has officially left the company's board following the annual shareholders meeting.
cards.body:
Reed Hastings, who co-founded Netflix and served as CEO for 25 years, has departed the company's board of directors. The departure took effect after the June 4 annual shareholders meeting, concluding his tenure as executive chairman.

Jay Hoag will become the new chairman of Netflix's board. Hastings led Netflix's transformation into the world's leading premium streaming service during his quarter-century as CEO before transitioning to the executive chairman role.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Season 8 Sets Peacock Viewership Record
cards.teaser: The reality dating show's new season reached 824 million minutes watched across its first three episodes, marking the platform's most-watched TV debut.
cards.body:
Season 8 of Love Island USA has become Peacock's most-watched debut for an original television season. The season premiered on June 2 and accumulated 824 million minutes watched across its first three episodes, marking a 74 percent increase over previous seasons.

Mobile viewing played a significant role in the season's success, with phones and tablets accounting for 23 percent of total viewership. This reflects a notable shift in how audiences consume reality television content on streaming platforms.

cards.headline: Sean Penn Skips Oscars Despite Winning Third Academy Award
cards.teaser: The actor won Best Supporting Actor at the 98th Academy Awards but was absent due to his refusal to attend large public gatherings.
cards.body:
Sean Penn did not attend the recent 98th Academy Awards despite winning Best Supporting Actor, his third Oscar. The actor revealed in a conversation with CNN that he refuses to attend public gatherings with more than eight people and declines all requests for selfies.

Penn's absence from the ceremony came as he maintained his longstanding policy against large public events. The win marked his third Academy Award over the course of his career.

cards.headline: Avatar: Fire and Ash Coming to Disney+ in June
cards.teaser: James Cameron's latest Pandora installment will stream alongside Pixar's Hoppers after successful theatrical runs.
cards.body:
Disney+ will add Avatar: Fire and Ash to its streaming library in June following the film's box office run. Director James Cameron's latest entry in the Avatar franchise expands the universe of Pandora after the success of Avatar and Avatar: The Way of Water, two of the highest-grossing films in cinema history.

Pixar's Hoppers will also arrive on the platform in June. The two releases represent major additions to Disney's streaming service following their theatrical windows.

cards.headline: Capcom Announces Resident Evil: Veronica Remake for 2027
cards.teaser: The remake of the 2000 survival horror game Code: Veronica will launch next year.
cards.body:
Capcom will release Resident Evil: Veronica in 2027, a remake of the 2000 game Resident Evil Code: Veronica. The announcement came during a gaming showcase event.

The original Code: Veronica took place three months after Resident Evil 2 and concurrently with Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. The story follows Claire Redfield, a character from the franchise's earlier installments.

hero.headline: Federal prosecutor opens election fraud investigations in California after Trump allegations
hero.body:
A federal prosecutor in California announced multiple investigations into alleged voter fraud following accusations by President Trump that Democrats engaged in misconduct during this week's primary elections. Bill Essayli, the first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, revealed the probes on Friday without disclosing specifics about what allegations are being examined.

The announcement came as California completed its gubernatorial primary election, where Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton competed for their party nominations to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Trump made public accusations of election fraud against Democrats in the state after primary voting concluded.

The Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles on Friday as Trump continued to claim that California Democrats were "rigging" the results. State officials have rejected the allegations, though the delay in election results has prompted concerns about misinformation regarding California's election integrity.

Election officials have explained that counting votes in California is taking longer than in other states due to the volume of ballots and processing procedures. Experts have warned that ballot counting could extend for weeks or even a month before final results are determined in the governor's race, the Los Angeles mayoral election, and congressional contests.

Essayli's announcement represents a notable development in the ongoing tensions between the Trump administration and California's Democratic leadership. The Central District of California, one of four federal judicial districts in the state, covers a significant portion of Southern California including Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, and Ventura counties.

Federal election fraud investigations are relatively uncommon and typically require substantial evidence of organized attempts to interfere with voting processes or ballot counting. The Justice Department has not disclosed information about the specific nature of the fraud allegations or which aspects of the primary election are under investigation.

The timing of the investigations, announced immediately after the primary and following presidential accusations, represents an unusual convergence of federal law enforcement activity and electoral politics. California has traditionally been a Democratic stronghold, and disputes between state officials and the Trump administration have become a consistent element of recent political dynamics. Trump has long promoted election conspiracy theories and made similar claims of fraud in previous elections without providing evidence.

cards.headline: Senate completes 18-hour voting session on immigration enforcement package
cards.teaser: The Senate concluded a marathon vote-a-rama on immigration enforcement legislation after nearly a full day of continuous voting.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a $70 billion immigration enforcement funding bill following an 18-hour overnight voting session. The Republican-backed legislation provides funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Border Patrol over the next three years.

The extended vote-a-rama session is a procedural feature of budget reconciliation bills that allows senators to propose unlimited amendments. Lawmakers worked through the night to complete votes on the enforcement package, with each individual vote taking only minutes.

cards.headline: Trump discusses fertilizer costs with Wisconsin farmers amid elevated prices
cards.teaser: President Trump met with farmers in Wisconsin to address rising fertilizer and fuel costs linked to the U.S. war in Iran.
cards.body:
President Trump held a roundtable with farmers in Wisconsin on Friday, focusing on skyrocketing fertilizer and energy prices that have resulted from the U.S. war in Iran. Trump told the farmers that fertilizer prices would decrease significantly, promising a return to levels from four months earlier.

During the event, Trump also discussed the Reflecting Pool and fountains, branching beyond the agricultural topics that formed the main purpose of the Wisconsin visit. The meeting came as farmers face increased input costs that affect their operations and profitability.

cards.headline: House Democrat calls for Maine candidate to exit Senate race over allegations
cards.teaser: Representative Madeleine Dean said Democrat Graham Platner has disqualified himself from the Maine Senate race amid allegations about his past behavior toward women.
cards.body:
Representative Madeleine Dean of Pennsylvania called Friday for Democrat Graham Platner to withdraw from the Maine Senate race, saying he has "disqualified himself" amid escalating allegations about his past behavior toward women.

Platner is denying accusations that he was physically rough with former girlfriends. He characterized the New York Times report and other controversies as signs his campaign is gaining momentum and indicated he will not exit the race.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: Deb Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico, advancing to the general election where she has an opportunity to make history. If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history.

Haaland previously served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration and represented New Mexico in the U.S. House of Representatives. Her primary victory sets up a general election race that could result in a historic milestone for Native American representation in state executive offices.

cards.headline: California gubernatorial primary results show Hilton and Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Early returns from California's governor primary show Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra leading their respective party contests to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California's gubernatorial primary results indicate Steve Hilton is leading among Republican candidates, while Xavier Becerra is ahead in the Democratic field. The race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom has attracted multiple prominent candidates from both parties.

On the Democratic side, Katie Porter and Tom Steyer are also competing for the nomination alongside Becerra. Republican Chad Bianco is challenging Hilton for the GOP nomination. The top finishers from each party will advance to the general election.

cards.headline: Former Border Patrol commander attended far-right international conference
cards.teaser: Greg Bovino, a former Border Patrol commander, spoke at an international far-right gathering that included white supremacists and neo-Nazis.
cards.body:
Greg Bovino, who previously commanded Border Patrol operations, recently appeared as a speaker at an international far-right conference. The gathering included attendees and speakers associated with white supremacist and neo-Nazi movements.

Bovino's participation in the event has drawn attention to his activities after leaving his position with Border Patrol. The conference brought together far-right figures from multiple countries.
